scientific_conclusion: The exact Stage-81 node-21 vertical-oblique sector maps are reconstructed from their already-fixed ordinates with zero numerical closure error. Every retained sector exceeds the preregistered 0.90 magnitude-weighted adjacent-ordinate coherence guard and the 0.75 within-sector cell-divergence retention guard: the minima are 0.960408 and 0.816746, respectively. The two fixed opposite-sector pairs retain 99.9182% and 99.9258% of their cell-divergence magnitude, so opposite-sector cancellation is not the explanation for the global cancellation. This supports only a frozen spatial cancellation/localization audit of those pair maps; it is not an adjoint sensitivity, does not justify changing the velocity rule, and does not rehabilitate the failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint.
positive_findings: The four inherited Stage-81 vertical-oblique sector maps are reconstructed exactly from their already-fixed individual ordinates without rebucketing the angular rule.
Magnitude-weighted adjacent-ordinate coherence and within-sector signed-retention are quantified separately so negligible boundary ordinates cannot dominate the coherence diagnosis.
All four retained vertical-oblique sectors satisfy the preregistered coherence and within-sector-retention guards.
negative_findings: Within-sector angular coherence is a frozen residual-structure diagnostic, not an adjoint sensitivity and not evidence that changing, pruning, moving, or reweighting velocity ordinates would improve q_av.
A high angular correlation does not constitute physical validation, and a low correlation by itself would not establish numerical error.
The failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint remains unrecovered and is not extended across Knudsen number.
No physical, collision, correction-floor, source-relaxation, transport, wall, normalization, or velocity-quadrature parameter is retuned, and no cavity solver is rerun.
The opposite-sector pair cell-divergence retention ratios are approximately 0.9992, so there is no supported opposite-sector cancellation mechanism at this level.
